challenge.back_up: proceed, revised twice in hand: the door is the system device's published tool.
challenge.better_approach: A bus verb on the system device was the other option the orchestrator named. Asking a box its own name must work with no bus, as on a Windows saveslate or a recovery install, so a published tool is the smaller path. Before Akien's line, platform.node() inside the tool or validation_store's copy were both on the table. Akien ruled that hostname comes from the system device.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That claude_identity.py:108 is the crash akiendell measured: the packet is unread, and akiendell's checkout may predate 4794006a7. That platform.node() is non-empty on Windows: it may return '' and the proof only runs on Linux. That the sieve's published_by_device check admits a tool nested at devices/<y>/tools/<t>/, which inspector.py:4783 _published_tool reads as exactly that.
challenge.prior_art: Consulted: the congruency lab, tickets grepped for 'uname', and git log -S uname. 4794006a7 already moved the call to rackmount.host_name (right home, wrong path). validation_store.host_name (cairn/tools/validation_store/validation_store.py:171) is a second copy with the same spelling, and B repoints it. The published-tool shape is copied from trouble/tools/store, db_domain/tools/client and librarian/tools/trees.
challenge.real_collision: None terminal. 4794006a7's rackmount docstring ('the os calls live HERE, in the system device') and Akien's line agree on the home. RULE 1 governs the path, and publishing reconciles the two. validation_store's copy collides with 'one door', which is B's to close.

answers.falsifier: Done when, with os.uname absent, who() returns a host that is non-empty, short and lowercased; claude_identity.py imports no cairn.devices module except cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host; and that tool's charter declares published_by_device. Wrong intent if akiendell's slate packet (C:\Users\akien\.akien\temp\akiendell_cc_0_slate_packet_20261120.json, unread because akiendell is offline) shows saveslate crashing somewhere other than claude_identity.
answers.from_idea: none, because it was cast straight from the measured crash site in cairn/tools/base/claude_identity.py (line 108 at 4794006a7^, "host": os.uname().nodename), which akiendelllinux_cc_orchestrator relayed on 2026-11-21 with no idea captured first
answers.how: Akien, relayed by akiendelllinux_cc_orchestrator on 2026-11-21: "hostname should come from the system device." system_rackmount publishes cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host/host.py, holding host_name() and os_id() moved out of rackmount.py, with a charter saying published_by_device: true. rackmount.py imports them back from inside the device. claude_identity imports that published module in place of rackmount.host_name, the unpublished import that saveslate auto-commit 4794006a7 added. A red-first proof deletes os.uname for one tooth and calls who(), and a second tooth checks that claude_identity imports no unpublished cairn.devices code.
answers.traces_to: RULE 1 (a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes: system_rackmount's public_interface is [], so 4794006a7's import is a breach); Law 8 (4794006a7 changed the line with no ticket and no proof); Law 3 (the Windows crash is measured at n=1 on akiendell, from a packet still unread)
answers.what: claude_identity.who() names this box's host on every OS Cairn runs on, Windows included, by asking the system device through the tool it publishes, so saveslate stops crashing on akiendell and no tool reaches unpublished device code.
